clue.text: Student challenge to wit at one time

definitions.meaning: at Oxford colleges a ... was a forfeit, a challenge to down a tankard of ale, imposed for a breach of table etiquette
in old usage a ... was the head, and so a person's brains or good sense

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are old university and archaic usage; 'at one time' signals that the second sense is no longer current.
explanation.definitionFit: Two dated senses: an Oxford dining forfeit, and an archaic word for the head or common sense.

clue.text: Avoid emphasising curious deaf spot on line

indicators.note: curious means odd, so the letters are made odd by rearranging

explanation.surface: Not drawing attention to a strange spot on the line where hearing fails.
explanation.walkthrough: On the piano the soft pedal mutes the notes, hence the figurative sense of toning something down; 'curious' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To soft-pedal is to play down, from the piano pedal that softens notes.

clue.text: Hazy cloud

definitions.meaning: to cloud is to make unclear, as a verb

explanation.definitionFit: Obscure as an adjective means vague, and as a verb means to cloud or hide.

clue.text: Shut down business-only the unions were taken in

definitions.text: only the unions were taken in

parts.note: shut down means closed
a shop is a business

explanation.surface: A firm closes because it only hired union members.
explanation.definitionFit: A closed shop is a workplace where only trade union members may be employed.

clue.text: Handcuff couple connected with obstruction

parts.note: a brace is a pair, as of game birds
let is an old word for a hindrance, surviving in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: A pair of prisoners chained together with something blocking their way.
explanation.definitionFit: Bracelets is slang for handcuffs, so one handcuff is a bracelet.

clue.text: Watches theatre diners?

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre
diners are eaters

explanation.surface: Keeping an eye on people dining at the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watches' looks like a verb but is a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeater is a watch that chimes the time when a button is pressed.

clue.text: A sound view to quote

indicators.note: sound here says the word is said out loud and heard as another spelling

parts.note: a view is a sight

explanation.surface: A good outlook worth mentioning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective for good, but signals a soundalike.
explanation.definitionFit: To cite is to quote a passage or source as evidence.

clue.text: After highball, say, writer one's found in bed

indicators.note: after says the writer's name follows the ball

parts.note: a lob is a high ball, as in tennis or cricket
Elia was the pen name of essayist Charles Lamb

explanation.surface: After a high-ball drink, a writer ends up in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'highball' suggests a cocktail; 'bed' is a flower bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobelia is a garden flower grown in beds and borders.

clue.text: Draw at home in Association?

parts.note: a draw is a tie in sport
in means at home

explanation.surface: A home draw in the Football Association.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie-in is a connection or link between things.

clue.text: Put together contract

definitions.meaning: to ... the brows is to draw them together, contracting them

explanation.definitionFit: Knit means join, and to knit one's brow is to wrinkle or contract it.

clue.text: Decorative chain of iron, with tin also inset

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: inset says one piece is set into another, here the word for also put within the symbol for tin

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
too means as well

explanation.surface: A description of a decorative chain made of iron with tin set into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A festoon is a garland or chain of flowers or ribbons hung in a curve as decoration.

clue.text: It's drinkable European accepts the bill

indicators.note: accepts says the first word takes the second inside it

parts.note: a Pole is a native of Poland, a European
a tab is a bill, as at a bar

explanation.surface: A Polish drinker agrees to pay the bar bill for something drinkable.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash in the printed clue separates the definition from the wordplay; 'accepts' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Potable is a formal synonym for drinkable, used of water fit to drink.

clue.text: With due care Mrs Grundy takes form for Latin

parts.note: Mrs Grundy, a character in an 18th-century play, became a byword for a narrow-minded, conventional prude

indicators.note: form is a verb here, as in to shape something anew, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A strait-laced woman fills in a form for a Latin course carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Grundy comes from Thomas Morton's 1798 play Speed the Plough, where neighbours keep asking what she will say; 'form' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Prudential describes acting with prudence, that is with careful forethought.

clue.text: Pastry dish left inside to cool

indicators.note: inside says the abbreviation goes within the verb

parts.note: to fan something is to cool it with moving air

explanation.surface: A tart left out to cool down.
explanation.definitionFit: A flan is an open pastry case with a sweet or savoury filling.

clue.text: Fancy £1 bonnet from America in all probability

parts.note: to fancy is to like
the pound sign is L (from Latin libra) and 1 is I in Roman numerals
a car's bonnet is called the hood in America

explanation.surface: Liking a cheap American hat, probably.
explanation.definitionFit: Likelihood is probability; in all likelihood means very probably.

clue.text: Surgical assistant's gown has openings for easy release

parts.note: a gown is a dress

indicators.note: openings means the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A theatre assistant's gown has easy-release fastenings.
explanation.definitionFit: A dresser is a surgeon's assistant who dresses wounds in hospital.

clue.text: Turned up in tailored trousers before start of event

indicators.note: tailored means made to fit, cut into a new shape
start of means the first letter

explanation.surface: Trousers are altered to have turn-ups before the event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' reads like trouser turn-ups in the surface, but describes a nose; 'tailored' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Retroussé, from French, describes a nose turned up at the tip.

clue.text: Remove hat and pipe for these last words

indicators.note: read as re-move, to move again, so the letters are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to take off your hat and put away your pipe before the final words.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitaph is an inscription on a tomb, the last words said about the dead.

clue.text: Composer has broken reed put in case

parts.note: Gustav Holst wrote The Planets

indicators.note: broken means the letters are smashed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician's reed is damaged and put in its case.
explanation.definitionFit: Holstered means placed in a holster, a case for a pistol.

clue.text: Forwards queueing here not allowed to score first

indicators.note: first says the word for score comes ahead of the other piece

parts.note: to score is to scratch a line
out means ruled out or disallowed

explanation.surface: Attackers waiting in a queue are told they may not score first.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby a line-out restarts play after the ball goes into touch: the forwards of both sides stand in two parallel lines while it is thrown in.
explanation.definitionFit: A line-out is the rugby set piece where forwards line up for the throw-in.

clue.text: Bunch of flowers with distinctive smell, and showy

parts.note: a wine's nose is its characteristic aroma
gay in its old sense means bright and showy

explanation.surface: A colourful bouquet with a striking scent.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosegay is a small posy of flowers, carried to smell sweet.

clue.text: An unusual Constable

definitions.meaning: a ... constable is a part-time volunteer police officer in Britain, often just called a ...

explanation.walkthrough: 'Constable' looks like the painter John Constable.
explanation.definitionFit: Special means exceptional, and a special is a British volunteer police officer.

clue.text: Live in, wearing proper dress when up

parts.note: in means wearing, as in dressed in black
a riding habit is the proper outfit when up on a horse

explanation.surface: To dwell somewhere while dressed properly when getting up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' means mounted on horseback, as a jockey is up.
explanation.definitionFit: To inhabit a place is to live in it.

clue.text: Glass frame made from initially seasoned wood

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: ash is a hardwood tree and its timber

explanation.surface: A window frame made from seasoned timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is the frame holding the glass panes of a window.

clue.text: On this ledge a woman may feel abandoned

definitions.text: On this ledge a woman may feel abandoned

parts.words: On this ledge a woman may feel abandoned
parts.note: a woman left unmarried was said to be left on a certain ledge, the place where unwanted things are put away

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'left on the shelf' describes someone, traditionally a woman, passed over for marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A shelf is a ledge, and being on it means being passed over.

clue.text: Does it go to one's head, sometimes having to tell lies?

definitions.text: Does it go to one's head, sometimes having to tell lies?

parts.words: Does it go to one's head, sometimes having to tell lies?
parts.note: a hat goes on the head; pork pies is rhyming slang for lies, so this hat's name contains a word for telling fibs

explanation.walkthrough: Pork pies (or porkies) is Cockney rhyming slang for lies; the clue describes headgear named after a meat pie.
explanation.definitionFit: A pork-pie hat is a man's felt hat with a flat round crown, shaped like the pie.

clue.text: Extra spurt of speed in punt

definitions.meaning: a burst of pace at the end of a race
a punt is a ... of a ball dropped from the hands

explanation.definitionFit: A kick is a finishing burst of speed, and to punt is to kick a ball.

clue.text: Business man's beginning a long sleep

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: beginning means the first letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A businessman's start to the day is a long lie-in.
explanation.definitionFit: A coma is a prolonged state of deep unconsciousness, likened to sleep.

clue.text: Write in large letters to grab attention

definitions.meaning: to ... a document is to copy it out in a large formal hand

explanation.definitionFit: Engross means both to write out formally in large script and to absorb wholly.

clue.text: Clothing sounds beat-up

definitions.meaning: British slang for clothes or gear

explanation.walkthrough: 'sounds' is a link: the word meaning clothing sounds like, being identical to, the word meaning beat up.
explanation.definitionFit: Clobber is slang both for clothes and for giving someone a beating.

clue.text: Quickly pass examination set in catchment area

parts.note: to fly is to pass quickly, as time flies
an exam paper is the set of questions

explanation.surface: Breeze through an exam in a geography topic on drainage basins.
explanation.definitionFit: Flypaper is a sticky strip that catches flies, so it is literally an area of catching.

clue.text: Prepared a paper, having dieted experimentally

indicators.note: experimentally suggests trying things out, so the letters are tried in a new order

explanation.surface: A journalist produced an article after trying a diet.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit a newspaper is to prepare it for publication.
